groups.description: Focused Hspec examples for the root package's console startup and exit integration.
Focused Hspec examples for the foundation package's Logging, Resources, Failures, Recovery, Workers, Messaging, and Time contracts.

Focused Hspec examples for the runtime package's application runner and lifecycle, logging lifetime, reporting, supervision, inbox services, package boundaries, resource smoke, and supervised messaging waits.

Headless Hspec examples for the GLFW package's session, window, command, control, host, dynamic window, monitor, input, and mode models over the test seam, its link declarations against the native manifest, and its package boundaries. Initializes no GLFW and needs no display.
Run the console executable's smoke mode end to end.

Focused Hspec examples for the Lua host package's fault and cancellation transport across the foreign-call boundary, stack and registry discipline, terminal close, independent execution under the threaded RTS, selectable standard libraries, and its export boundary. Deliberate nontermination is a separate local-only probe.

Local-only optional Linux confinement and resource-limit feasibility probe (LUA-14). Launches confined children through the candidate namespace, private-root, and seccomp profile; records the machine, the permissions, and whether the profile installed at all; and checks the fail-closed refusal, the denied native and Lua accesses with the mechanism that denied each, two-instance isolation and independent termination, the whole-process memory ceiling, the execution bound's escalation, and the three lifetime cases. Built and run on Linux only; on other platforms the components are not built. A green run is evidence, never a supported-platform verdict.

Portable Hspec contracts for the GPU retention and frame-ownership model: typed identities and the misuse they are rejected as, the hold ledger and disposal eligibility, frame ownership phases and their obligations, validated admission budgets and their backpressure, recovery and allocation-retry accounting, and bounded round-robin owner progress under a scripted clock. It runs through the CPU project and needs no Vulkan SDK.

Portable Hspec contracts for the Vulkan diagnostic capture: the production C capture storage driven through its package-local producer entry — bounded copying under one shared text budget and an object limit, error latching ahead of admission, saturation with its drop counter, truncation and capture-failure counting, contained producer failures, and concurrent producers — and the diagnostic lifetime around it: delivery through the caller's logger by a worker in a group of its own, the verdict, sink failure beside a preserved primary failure, and teardown ordering on every exit. It runs through the CPU project and needs no Vulkan SDK.

Vulkan-linked headless Hspec contracts, executed rather than only built, through cabal.project.vulkan against the provisioned native prefix: the native backend's profile and roots decisions over a stand-in native layer (native-tests), its shader contract against the provisioned compiler (shader-tests), and the window integration's controller over the GLFW package's scripted seam (integration-tests). None acquires a display, a GLFW session, or a device, and none reads desktop consent; the headers and loader are build and link prerequisites only.

The Vulkan native suite: the package-native fixture's shared roots under the graphics owner, with GLFW's session on the process main thread, and the migrated VK-2, VK-5, VK-6 and VK-7 cases and the synchronization-validation control in private child processes, all with the validation layer and synchronization validation enabled, failing on any validation error or incomplete diagnostic capture after the last teardown. Its executable is built in a separate preparation stage; its native execution — test-owned display, fixtures, examples, retirement, diagnostic finalization and teardown — is measured alone under a 30-second watchdog. On Linux the command starts its own isolated X11 display; on macOS it needs the human's per-session desktop consent.

Hspec examples driving the documentation landing helper, this planner and runner, the CI image builder, and the native recipe helper against temporary Git repositories; the local test/flake lab's selection, durable history, recovery, process guardians, exports, and skill installation; and the boundary that keeps the Vulkan project out of the mandatory floor, holds its two groups to their commands and routing, and holds the compatibility summary to the retained records it quotes.

Local-only optional headless X11 helper probes using stub servers and window managers, including real 30-second startup deadlines. Never selected automatically or routed to CI; eligible for coordinated local testing. Opens no desktop session.
Real GLFW session, thread, and window examples through the shared native Hspec fixture, on an isolated X11 display.

The native suite's Wayland-only examples, on the isolated headless compositor tools/display/wayland.sh starts: that a session requesting Wayland selected Wayland on the socket its consent authorized, and that both X11 test-check drivers answer unavailable there without provoking a GLFW report. Optional and requested by name; the selector names that group and nothing else.
command: --test-option=/GLFW native/the shared session/on an isolated Wayland session/

groups.description: LUA-15's local macOS feasibility proof: a confined helper's denied filesystem, network, process, and native-module accesses before and after its mod source loads, two-instance process and storage isolation, the enforced whole-process memory limit and the execution bound, and the three lifetime endings. Optional and Darwin-only; the component is not built elsewhere, so a request for it on Linux fails rather than passing vacuously.
Local-only optional headless Wayland helper probes using stub compositor and client programs, including the real readiness deadline. Opens no desktop session.
Local-only optional nonterminating-Lua cancellation experiment. Deliberately exhausts a five-second observation window in a child process; ordinary Lua contracts remain in lua-host-tests.
